newsitem.title: INDIA: India's 96/97 economic growth seen at six percent.
newsitem.headline: India's 96/97 economic growth seen at six percent.

text.p: A recovery in the agriculture sector will offset a slowdown in industrial growth and help India post gross domestic product growth of six percent in 1996/97 (April-March), analysts said on Sunday.
This compares with an official target of GDP growth at 6.5 percent in the current fiscal year ending March 31, after an expansion of 6.6 percent in 1995/96.
"I would estimate GDP to grow at about six percent," Ashok Gulati, economist at the National Council of Applied Economic Research (NCAER), an independent think-tank, told Reuters.

Analysts said a slowdown in policy reforms, a dip in industrial growth, political uncertainty, a lull in investment activities and infrastructural bottlenecks were combining to hold back GDP growth in 1996/97.

"The slowing down of policy reforms and lack of basic infrastructure will make it difficult to achieve a GDP growth of over six percent," S.P. Gupta, director of the Indian Council for Research on International Economic Relations (ICRIER), told Reuters.
Growth in 1996/97 would be led by the agriculture sector which was expected to grow at about four percent, analysts said.
India's farm sector grew at 0.9 percent in 1995/96.
"The growth in (the) agricultural sector will be about 4.5 percent," said D.H. Pai Panandikar, an economist and corporate policy adviser.
Agriculture ministry officials have said the outlook for foodgrain production in 1996/97 is bright and output likely to reach 197 million tonnes compared with 185 million tonnes the previous year.
"The distribution of rainfall has been very good this year," Panandikar said.
India, predominantly an agricultural country, had its ninth good monsoon in a row in 1996. The farm sector employs about two-thirds of India's workforce and accounts for one-third of its GDP.
"The slowdown in industry, especially (the) infrastructure sector, is a cause for worry," ICRIER's Gupta said
"I do not see a major pick-up in industrial growth in the coming months of the current fiscal year," Panandikar said.
Business leaders last week told Reuters that the industrial sector would grow at eight percent in 1996/97 against an official target of 12 percent.
"Political instability is hindering investment and reforms," NCAER's Gulati said.
Indian industry grew at 12.1 percent in 1995/96.
But the Industry Ministry said on Thursday that industrial growth in the current fiscal year would be above 10 percent.
Analysts said the overall slowdown in industry would also affect the services sector.
"The services sector cannot maintain the momentum achieved last year," Gupta said.
India's hotels, trade, transport and communication industry notched up growth of 10.1 percent in 1995/96 compared to 8.0 percent the previous year.
The financial sector -- insurance, real estate and business services and finance -- grew at 5.6 percent in 1995/96 against 4.3 percent the preceding year.
"The government has to remove uncertainty in policy making and improve basic infrastructure services to achieve a GDP growth of 6.5 percent and beyond," Gupta said.
India has set a target of accelerated seven percent annual economic growth for its ninth five-year plan beginning on April 1, 1997.
